A city prominent under Hammurabi, who made it the capital of Babylonia.
Best known for his law code.

The age of pyramids reached its zenith at Giza.

The southern kingdom was conquered by the Babylonians.
Critics claimed the Hittites were an error in the Bible. Archaeology verified biblical references and historians practiced revisionism.

Rule by a monarch, a king or queen; may involve a royal family.

Civilization on the island of Crete, characterized by prosperous trade.

A commercial and sea-faring community.
Similar to modern totalitarian states, with the individual subordinated to the state.

Greek city-states called truces during the games. Originally men only.

Associated with both deductive and inductive reasoning.
Transitioned chronologically from a republic to a dictator to an empire.
Council of nobles (senators) from the Patrician class who held their positions for life.

Responsible for the death or enslavement of over one million people.

Had legislation against adultery (he was exempt).
The Roman peace.
A sharing of power among four rulers.
Met his militarily superior enemy at the Milvian Bridge outside Rome and prevailed.
Moved the capital of the Roman Empire to Byzantium, renamed Constantinople.
Laid waste to Jerusalem; the Temple was destroyed.
The Roman Empire fell only in the West; the Eastern half lived on.
No single explanation accounts for Rome’s decline; multiple forces operated concurrently.

Asserted that Jesus never lived, but rather that He was “invented.”
Roman historian whose Roman Annals mention Nero blaming Christians for the fire of Rome; he also describes Christ’s execution.

Full religious freedom throughout the Roman Empire.
Sought to defend or explain Christianity.
Attacked heretical ideas.

Muslim empire of the Turks; ultimately captured Constantinople.
Strategically located for commercial and political influence.

Suffering is necessary, according to this doctrine, because the person has not made complete satisfaction for sins.
Communion, the heart of the Mass worship service.
At the priest’s words, the elements actually become the body and blood of Christ, according to the RCC doctrine.
Ordination; priests are sanctioned for their work by a bishop.
“Last Rites” given by a priest to someone near death for forgiveness of sins.
In general, has no gods and is based on Four Noble Truths.

May be described as “Intuitive Mysticism,” with intuitive meaning without rational analysis.
Added important dimensions to Confucian thought in human nature (man is good) and government (should be concerned for the welfare of people).
Embraces a pragmatic (practical as opposed to idealistic) approach; people were considered basically bad, so strict laws were necessary.
Not a united, monolithic entity; outward conformity but inward dissension.

Established custom, normative precedent, conduct, and cumulative tradition, typically based on Muhammad’s example.
God’s eternal and immutable will for humanity, expressed in the Quran and Muhammad’s example; ideal Islamic law.

Shrine in Mecca, also spelled Kaaba or Ka’ba.
The migration of Muhammad and his followers, which became the starting year for the Muslim calendar.

The right of an eldest son to succeed to his father’s estate to the exclusion of all his siblings.
The buying and selling of spiritual or Church benefits.
Established his rule over much of the former Roman Empire in Europe.
Norsemen who made their home in Scandinavia (Norway, Sweden, Denmark).
A decentralized political relationship among nobles.

An economic relationship between nobles and serfs; the serfs lived on the lord’s manor.
A political entity centered in the German states and Northern Italy.
Became king of England; ruled in France and England, not as Holy Roman Emperor.
Conflict over kings’ claim to appoint bishops and abbots; simony and primogeniture were related to investiture.
The desire to earn salvation (all past sins would be forgiven).
Increased conflict between Eastern and Western churches.
“An indulgence is partial or plenary according as it removes either part or all of the temporal punishment due to sin.”
Likely the most powerful pope; the height of papal power.
The idea that law is above the king, placing limits on royal power.
Likely a combination of bubonic and pneumonic plagues.
The plague appeared in waves, rather than continuously.
A bacterium, yersinia pestis.
One pope in Rome and one in Avignon, each with his own cardinals.

Established England and France as clearly distinct nations.
Henry Tudor won this conflict.
A crusade designed to oust Muslims who had invaded Spain.
A French word meaning “rebirth.”
The Renaissance moved across the Alps into northern Europe.

Less emphasis on the religious and supernatural, more on things of the earthly world.
A school of thought emphasizing the importance and self-expression of the individual.
Italian church, business, and government leaders possessed disposable income for patronage (sponsorship) of the arts.
The cultural center or “heart” of Renaissance life.
A true “Renaissance Man” (multi-talented).
Dutch scholar referred to as the “Prince of Humanists.”

1st successful English settlement in North America – Jamestown, VA

A large-hulled ship to carry cargo; Spanish galleons were intercepted and thus guns were added.
The overland trade route to Asia was hindered by the Ottoman Turks, so a sea route was desired.
A Portuguese ship with sails for sailing into a headwind; it was fast.
God, Greed, & Glory.

Sailed around Africa, continued to India, and returned.
Genoese sailor who convinced Queen Isabella of Castile to support him; believed he had landed in Asia.
Conquered the great Aztec Empire in Mexico.
His crew returned to Spain having circumnavigated the globe.
Conquered the Inca Empire in Peru.
Spain’s settlements grew into colonies with the sole purpose of bolstering the Spanish economy.
Spain developed a convoy system of guard ships and galleons to make voyages safer.
Oldest city in the U.S., according to the packet.
Few French people moved to North America, and many who did eventually left.
England’s first permanent settlement; tobacco was its cash crop.
Also called Separatists; stepped ashore at what we call Plymouth, Massachusetts.
Settled the Massachusetts Bay Colony.
Searched for a Northwest Passage.
Native cultures were undermined.
The exchange of Old and New World plants, animals, and diseases.

Henry VIII confirmed as supreme head (on earth) of the C. of E.
Council of Trent & the Catholic Counter-Reformation

Corruption in the RCC; monarchs strong enough to challenge church power; popularity of mysticism; a new intellectual climate.

Began indulgence sales in German lands, the immediate cause of the Reformation.
Academic points for scholarly debate, written by Martin Luther.

Education, winning back areas from Protestantism, and foreign missions.
Executed for adultery.

Lutheran, Anglican, Reformed, Anabaptist.
